title: Thermal Properties of Matter
syllabus: Heat, temperature, thermal expansion; specific heat capacity, calorimetry; change of state, latent heat capacity; Heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation, thermal conductivity, Newton's law of cooling, Stefan's law, Wien's displacement law, Green house effect

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A body cools from $80^\circ\text{C}$ to $60^\circ\text{C}$ in 5 minutes when the ambient temperature is $20^\circ\text{C}$. The time taken by the body to cool from $60^\circ\text{C}$ to $40^\circ\text{C}$ in the same surroundings will be:
questions.solution:
Using Newton's law of cooling in approximate form: $\frac{T_1 - T_2}{t} = K\left(\frac{T_1 + T_2}{2} - T_0\right)$.
For cooling from $80^\circ\text{C}$ to $60^\circ\text{C}$ in $5\text{ min}$ with $T_0 = 20^\circ\text{C}$:
$$\frac{80 - 60}{5} = K(70 - 20) \implies 4 = 50K \implies K = \frac{4}{50} = \frac{2}{25}$$
For cooling from $60^\circ\text{C}$ to $40^\circ\text{C}$ in time $t$:
$$\frac{60 - 40}{t} = K(50 - 20) \implies \frac{20}{t} = \left(\frac{2}{25}\right)(30) = \frac{12}{5}$$
$$t = \frac{20 \times 5}{12} = \frac{100}{12} \approx 8.33\text{ min}$$
Using exact exponential form: $\ln\left(\frac{T - T_0}{T_i - T_0}\right) = -kt$.
$\ln(40/60) = -5k \implies k = \frac{1}{5}\ln(1.5) \approx 0.08109\text{ min}^{-1}$.
For $60^\circ\text{C}$ to $40^\circ\text{C}$: $\ln(20/40) = -kt \implies \ln(2) = kt \implies t = \frac{0.69315}{0.08109} \approx 8.55\text{ to } 9.2\text{ min}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Three rods of identical cross-sectional area and made of the same material form an equilateral triangle $ABC$. If heat is supplied at vertex $A$ at a constant rate and vertices $B$ and $C$ are kept at constant temperature $0^\circ\text{C}$, the temperature at the midpoint of branch $BC$ in steady state is:
questions.solution:
Vertices $B$ and $C$ are held at identical boundary temperature $T_B = T_C = 0^\circ\text{C}$.
Along rod $BC$, both ends are at $0^\circ\text{C}$. With no internal heat generation or heat loss, in the steady state, the temperature profile along $BC$ must be uniform and equal to $0^\circ\text{C}$ throughout.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The peak wavelength $\lambda_m$ emitted by a black body at temperature $T_1 = 2000\text{ K}$ is $1.5\,\mu\text{m}$. If the temperature of the black body is increased to $T_2 = 3000\text{ K}$, the peak wavelength shifts to:
questions.solution:
By Wien's displacement law, $\lambda_m T = b = \text{constant}$:
$$\lambda_{m1} T_1 = \lambda_{m2} T_2$$
$$(1.5\,\mu\text{m})(2000\text{ K}) = \lambda_{m2}(3000\text{ K})$$
$$\lambda_{m2} = \frac{3000}{3000} = 1.0\,\mu\text{m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A bimetallic strip consists of two metal strips $A$ and $B$ of equal length welded together. Their linear expansion coefficients satisfy $\alpha_A > \alpha_B$. When the strip is heated uniformly, it will:
options: Bend with metal $A$ on the convex side
Bend with metal $B$ on the convex side
questions.solution:
Since $\alpha_A > \alpha_B$, strip $A$ expands more than strip $B$ for the same temperature rise $\Delta T$.
To accommodate the greater arc length, metal $A$ must be on the outer (convex) curvature and metal $B$ on the inner (concave) curvature.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Two spheres of the same material have radii $1\text{ m}$ and $4\text{ m}$ and temperatures $4000\text{ K}$ and $2000\text{ K}$ respectively. The ratio of energy radiated per second by the first sphere to that by the second is:
questions.solution:
From Stefan-Boltzmann law, radiant power is $E = \sigma e A T^4 = \sigma e (4\pi R^2) T^4 \propto R^2 T^4$.
$$\frac{E_1}{E_2} = \left(\frac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^2 \left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^4 = \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2 \left(\frac{4000}{2000}\right)^4 = \frac{1}{16} \times 2^4 = \frac{16}{16} = 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Two rods of the same length $L$ and identical cross-sectional area $A$ are joined in series. Their thermal conductivities are $K_1$ and $K_2$. The equivalent thermal conductivity $K_{\text{eq}}$ of the combination is:
questions.solution:
In series combination, the thermal resistances add up: $R_{\text{eq}} = R_1 + R_2$.
$$\frac{2L}{K_{\text{eq}} A} = \frac{L}{K_1 A} + \frac{L}{K_2 A} \implies \frac{2}{K_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{1}{K_1} + \frac{1}{K_2} = \frac{K_1 + K_2}{K_1 K_2}$$
$$K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{2 K_1 K_2}{K_1 + K_2}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] If $10\text{ g}$ of ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is mixed with $10\text{ g}$ of water at $40^\circ\text{C}$, the final equilibrium temperature of the mixture is (take $L_f = 80\text{ cal/g}$, $s_w = 1\text{ cal/g}\cdot^\circ\text{C}$):
questions.solution:
Heat required to melt all ice completely at $0^\circ\text{C}$:
$$Q_{\text{req}} = m_{\text{ice}} L_f = 10 \times 80 = 800\text{ cal}$$
Maximum heat released by cooling water from $40^\circ\text{C}$ to $0^\circ\text{C}$:
$$Q_{\text{avail}} = m_w s_w \Delta T = 10 \times 1 \times 40 = 400\text{ cal}$$
Since $Q_{\text{avail}} < Q_{\text{req}}$, only a fraction of the ice melts ($m_{\text{melted}} = \frac{400}{80} = 5\text{ g}$).
The system remains in phase equilibrium at $0^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A metal rod of length $L_0$ and linear expansion coefficient $\alpha$ is placed on a smooth horizontal table. If its temperature is raised by $\Delta T$, the longitudinal thermal stress developed inside the rod is:
questions.solution:
Thermal stress develops only when the free thermal expansion of a body is constrained or prevented by rigid boundaries.
Because the rod is placed on a smooth horizontal surface without any external constraint, it expands freely ($\Delta L = L_0 \alpha \Delta T$) and the internal thermal stress is identically zero.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The ratio of emissive power to absorptive power for radiation at a given wavelength and temperature is identical for all bodies and equals the emissive power of a perfect black body. This fundamental radiation statement is:
questions.solution: Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation states that at thermal equilibrium, the ratio of emissive power ($e_\lambda$) to absorptive power ($a_\lambda$) of a body is a universal function of wavelength and temperature, equal to the emissive power of an ideal black body: $\frac{e_\lambda}{a_\lambda} = E_\lambda$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A cylindrical steel rod of length $1\text{ m}$ is heated so that its temperature changes by $100^\circ\text{C}$. If the ends are prevented from expanding by rigid supports, the strain energy stored per unit volume of the rod is (take $Y = 2 \times 10^{11}\text{ N/m}^2$, $\alpha = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1}$):
questions.solution:
Thermal strain is $\varepsilon = \alpha \Delta T = (1.2 \times 10^{-5})(100) = 1.2 \times 10^{-3}$.
Thermal stress is $\sigma = Y \varepsilon = (2 \times 10^{11})(1.2 \times 10^{-3}) = 2.4 \times 10^8\text{ N/m}^2$.
Elastic strain energy stored per unit volume is:
$$u = \frac{1}{2} \sigma \varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} (2.4 \times 10^8)(1.2 \times 10^{-3}) = 1.44 \times 10^5\text{ J/m}^3$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A pendulum clock has a brass pendulum rod. It keeps correct time at $20^\circ\text{C}$. If $\alpha = 2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ }^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$, how much time does the clock lose or gain per day at $40^\circ\text{C}$?
questions.solution:
Fractional variation in time period is $\frac{\Delta T}{T} = \frac{1}{2} \alpha \Delta\theta$.
At higher temperature ($40^\circ\text{C} > 20^\circ\text{C}$), the length increases, $T$ increases, and the clock runs slow (loses time):
$$\Delta t = \frac{1}{2} \alpha \Delta\theta \times (86400\text{ s}) = \frac{1}{2}(2 \times 10^{-5})(20)(86400) = 2 \times 10^{-4} \times 86400 = 17.28\text{ s/day}$$

questions.question: A cavity with a tiny pinhole is maintained at a constant temperature $T$. The radiation escaping from the pinhole behaves as:
questions.solution: A hollow enclosure (cavity) kept at uniform temperature with a small opening acts as a Ferry's black body; any radiation exiting the pinhole is authentic black body radiation with a continuous Planckian spectrum.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A composite slab consists of two parallel layers of thicknesses $d_1$ and $d_2$ with thermal conductivities $K_1$ and $K_2$ placed in series. The junction temperature between the slabs when the outer faces are held at temperatures $T_1$ and $T_2$ ($T_1 > T_2$) is:
questions.solution:
In steady state, heat current $H$ passing through both layers is identical:
$$H = \frac{K_1 A(T_1 - T_j)}{d_1} = \frac{K_2 A(T_j - T_2)}{d_2}$$
$$\frac{K_1}{d_1} T_1 - \frac{K_1}{d_1} T_j = \frac{K_2}{d_2} T_j - \frac{K_2}{d_2} T_2$$
$$T_j \left(\frac{K_1}{d_1} + \frac{K_2}{d_2}\right) = \frac{K_1 T_1}{d_1} + \frac{K_2 T_2}{d_2} \implies T_j = \frac{\frac{K_1 T_1}{d_1} + \frac{K_2 T_2}{d_2}}{\frac{K_1}{d_1} + \frac{K_2}{d_2}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A solid copper cube of edge length $a$ and a solid copper sphere of radius $a$ are heated to the same high temperature and allowed to cool in the same surroundings. The initial ratio of their rates of cooling $\left(-\frac{dT}{dt}\right)_{\text{cube}} : \left(-\frac{dT}{dt}\right)_{\text{sphere}}$ is:
questions.solution:
Rate of cooling is $-\frac{dT}{dt} = \frac{e \sigma A (T^4 - T_0^4)}{m s} = \frac{e \sigma (T^4 - T_0^4)}{\rho s} \left(\frac{A}{V}\right)$.
For the cube: $A = 6a^2$, $V = a^3 \implies \frac{A}{V} = \frac{6}{a}$.
For the sphere of radius $a$: $A = 4\pi a^2$, $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi a^3 \implies \frac{A}{V} = \frac{3}{a}$.
$$\frac{(-dT/dt)_{\text{cube}}}{(-dT/dt)_{\text{sphere}}} = \frac{6/a}{3/a} = 2 : 1$$
Wait, option (1) is $2:1$ which is option B. Checking option A, B: Option B is $2:1$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An iron tire is to be fitted onto a wooden cartwheel of diameter $1.0\text{ m}$. The inner diameter of the tire is $6\text{ mm}$ smaller than that of the wheel at $20^\circ\text{C}$. The temperature to which the tire must be heated to slip over the wheel is (take $\alpha_{\text{iron}} = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ }^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$):
questions.solution:
Required change in diameter is $\Delta d = 6\text{ mm} = 6 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$.
Initial diameter $d_0 = 1.0 - 0.006 = 0.994\text{ m} \approx 1.0\text{ m}$.
$$\Delta d = d_0 \alpha \Delta T$$
$$6 \times 10^{-3} = 1.0 \times (1.2 \times 10^{-5}) \Delta T \implies \Delta T = \frac{6 \times 10^{-3}}{1.2 \times 10^{-5}} = 500^\circ\text{C}$$
Final temperature $T = T_0 + \Delta T = 20 + 500 = 520^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The anomalous expansion of water occurs over the temperature interval:
questions.solution: Between $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $4^\circ\text{C}$, water contracts upon heating (its density increases, reaching a maximum value at $4^\circ\text{C}$); this is its anomalous thermal behaviour.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A beaker contains water up to height $H$. If the coefficient of volume expansion of water is $\gamma$ and that of linear expansion of the beaker material is $\alpha$, the liquid level will remain unchanged upon heating when:
questions.solution:
Height of the liquid column is $h = \frac{V}{A}$.
Fractional change in height:
$$\frac{\Delta h}{h} = \frac{\Delta V}{V} - \frac{\Delta A}{A} = \gamma \Delta T - (2\alpha) \Delta T = (\gamma - 2\alpha)\Delta T$$
For the liquid level to remain constant ($\Delta h = 0$):
$$\gamma = 2\alpha$$

questions.question: A metal sheet has a hole of diameter $D$ punched through it. When the sheet is heated uniformly:
options: The diameter may increase or decrease depending on the sheet area
questions.solution: Thermal expansion resembles a photographic enlargement. Every linear dimension of the body increases uniformly, so the distance between any two points on the boundary of the hole increases, expanding the diameter $D$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A thermos bottle contains coffee at $90^\circ\text{C}$. The primary mechanism by which heat is lost from the thermos to the room through the vacuum jacket is:
questions.solution: The evacuated double walls eliminate heat transfer by conduction and convection because both require a material medium. Heat can traverse the vacuum space purely via thermal radiation.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A black body radiates $20\text{ W}$ at temperature $227^\circ\text{C}$. If its temperature is raised to $727^\circ\text{C}$, the power radiated by it will be:
questions.solution:
Temperatures in Kelvin:
$T_1 = 227 + 273 = 500\text{ K}$, $T_2 = 727 + 273 = 1000\text{ K}$.
By Stefan's law: $P \propto T^4$.
$$\frac{P_2}{P_1} = \left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^4 = \left(\frac{1000}{500}\right)^4 = (2)^4 = 16$$
$$P_2 = 16 \times 20\text{ W} = 320\text{ W}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A copper calorimeter of mass $100\text{ g}$ contains $150\text{ g}$ of water in thermal equilibrium at $20^\circ\text{C}$. A metallic piece of mass $200\text{ g}$ at $100^\circ\text{C}$ is dropped into the calorimeter. If the final steady temperature of the mixture is $30^\circ\text{C}$, find the specific heat capacity of the metal piece in $\text{cal}/(\text{g}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$ (take specific heat of copper $= 0.1\text{ cal}/(\text{g}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$ and water $= 1.0\text{ cal}/(\text{g}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Heat gained by water and calorimeter:
$$Q_{\text{gain}} = (m_w s_w + m_c s_c)\Delta T_1 = (150 \times 1 + 100 \times 0.1)(30 - 20) = (150 + 10)(10) = 1600\text{ cal}$$
Heat lost by the metal piece:
$$Q_{\text{loss}} = m_m s_m (100 - 30) = 200 \times s_m \times 70 = 14000 s_m$$
By principle of calorimetry:
$$14000 s_m = 1600 \implies s_m = \frac{1600}{14000} = \frac{8}{70} = \frac{4}{35} \approx 0.114\text{ cal}/(\text{g}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] An iron rod of length $50\text{ cm}$ and a brass rod of length $L_2$ have a difference in their lengths that remains invariant at all temperatures. If $\alpha_{\text{iron}} = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1}$ and $\alpha_{\text{brass}} = 1.8 \times 10^{-5}\text{ K}^{-1}$, find the length $L_2$ (in cm) of the brass rod (rounded to one decimal place).
questions.solution:
Condition for invariant length difference at all temperatures:
$$\Delta L_1 = \Delta L_2 \implies L_1 \alpha_1 \Delta T = L_2 \alpha_2 \Delta T$$
$$L_2 = L_1 \left(\frac{\alpha_1}{\alpha_2}\right) = 50\text{ cm} \times \left(\frac{1.2 \times 10^{-5}}{1.8 \times 10^{-5}}\right) = 50 \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{100}{3} \approx 33.33\text{ cm} \approx 33.3\text{ cm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A metal bar of length $0.2\text{ m}$ and cross-sectional area $1.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}^2$ has its two ends maintained at $100^\circ\text{C}$ and $0^\circ\text{C}$ respectively. If its thermal conductivity is $400\text{ W}/(\text{m}\cdot\text{K})$, find the rate of heat flow (in Watts) through the bar in steady state.
questions.solution:
Rate of heat flow by Fourier's law:
$$\frac{dQ}{dt} = \frac{K A \Delta T}{L}$$
$$\frac{dQ}{dt} = \frac{400 \times (1.0 \times 10^{-4}) \times (100 - 0)}{0.2} = \frac{400 \times 10^{-4} \times 100}{0.2} = \frac{4}{0.2} = 20.0\text{ W}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An electric heater delivers a steady power of $1000\text{ W}$ to $2\text{ kg}$ of water in an insulated vessel. Find the time (in seconds) taken to heat the water from $20^\circ\text{C}$ to $100^\circ\text{C}$ (take specific heat capacity of water $= 4200\text{ J}/(\text{kg}\cdot^\circ\text{C})$).
questions.solution:
Thermal energy required:
$$Q = m s \Delta T = 2\text{ kg} \times 4200\text{ J}/(\text{kg}\cdot^\circ\text{C}) \times (100 - 20) = 8400 \times 80 = 672000\text{ J}$$
Time required:
$$t = \frac{Q}{P} = \frac{672000\text{ J}}{1000\text{ W}} = 672.0\text{ s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A spherical black body of radius $10\text{ cm}$ radiates $450\text{ W}$ at temperature $500\text{ K}$. If the radius is halved and temperature is doubled, find the power radiated (in Watts).
questions.solution:
Radiated power from a sphere is given by $P = \sigma (4\pi R^2) T^4 \propto R^2 T^4$.
$$\frac{P'}{P} = \left(\frac{R'}{R}\right)^2 \left(\frac{T'}{T}\right)^4 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 (2)^4 = \frac{1}{4} \times 16 = 4$$
$$P' = 4 \times P = 4 \times 450\text{ W} = 1800.0\text{ W}$$
